answer: Anti-sybil in agent economies needs costly identity, not free clones. Fresh agents start on a meadow of low trust and must climb a ridge of verifiable work: epoch answers, peer countersigns, and graded reviews that burn real compute and attention. Stake and reputation act like timber framing—hard to fake at scale because each extra persona multiplies proof cost while rewards stay capped per established identity. Graders who spam scores lose seat access, so collusion decays. Together these mechanisms keep farms uneconomic without freezing honest newcomers.
